missed_problems: No schema/contract validation between stages (LLM tags flow straight into the cutter, so non-deterministic model output silently corrupts downstream cuts and is the likely root cause of the wrong outro)
No observability: per-stage latency, cost, and error budgets are untracked, so the 16s desync was only caught after the fact instead of via a frame-locked master timeline alarm
Human judge is an un-SLA'd synchronous bottleneck with no async queue, parallel reviewers, or escalation path — the real bottleneck that won't survive beyond a handful of tours

automation_priorities.item: Single-pass render compositor (VO + footage + music + SRT burned in one ffmpeg/compositor call, VO as the master timeline anchor)
automation_priorities.reason: Eliminates 3 of the 5 reported defects at once: desync, lost subs, and audio mix churn. One deterministic pass is the cheapest ROI in the entire pipeline.

automation_priorities.item: Strict JSON schema gates between every stage (fetch → tag → cut → render) with parser fuzz tests on real stock SRTs/VTTs
automation_priorities.reason: The 1/8 SRT cue bug and wrong outro are upstream validation failures, not render failures. Schema-locked contracts make the LLM deterministic and catch drift early.

automation_priorities.item: Async human judge queue with SLA, parallel reviewers, and a confidence-based auto-approve threshold from the LLM tagger
automation_priorities.reason: Human review must be an exception path, not the default. Auto-approve high-confidence cuts; reserve humans for low-confidence/outlier cases.

automation_priorities.item: Asset pre-flight validator (duration, codec, loudness/LUFS, license metadata, checksum) before anything enters the timeline
automation_priorities.reason: Prevents the 'inspect external assets' lesson from being learned manually every time; turns it into an enforced gate.

automation_priorities.item: M3 QA as a blocking gate with structured auto-fix rules (re-render, swap asset, regenerate outro) feeding back into the orchestrator
automation_priorities.reason: M3 should not just report — it should drive a closed-loop remediation, capping retries to avoid the 4-iteration audio mix spiral.

scale_risks: Stock API rate limits and per-asset licensing cost explode linearly per tour; no caching/dedupe layer mentioned
LLM token cost and latency grow with tour complexity; no prompt caching or model-tier routing (small model for tags, large only for script)
Human judge queue becomes the system bottleneck at 100+ tours/day even with parallelism; cost-per-review will dominate
M3 QA compute cost scales with render minutes; no incremental/sample-based audit strategy disclosed
Localization: SRT/subs per language multiplies render passes unless architected as parameterized single-pass
Asset storage growth (raw stock + intermediates + finals) with no retention/cleanup policy will balloon
No version pinning on LLM/M3 → silent quality regressions when upstream models update
No render-failure replay or partial-render recovery; one bad stock clip kills the whole tour

cursor_architecture.one_command: tour_url → finished video: ingest validates URL+metadata against schema → parallel stock/audio/sub fetcher with dedupe → asset pre-flight (codec, duration, LUFS, license) → LLM tagger emits schema-locked JSON (temperature=0, pinned model) → async judge queue auto-approves ≥0.85 confidence else human → timeline planner pins VO as master clock and back-derives cuts/sub timings → single-pass compositor (ffmpeg/compositor) renders VO+footage+music+burned subs in one call with LUFS normalization → M3 QA gate runs structured checks and auto-fixes up to 2 retries → orchestrator publishes to storage + logs cost/latency/SLA metrics → returns finished video URL
key_modules: timeline-anchor-planner (VO as master clock, derives all cuts/subs)
orchestrator (durable execution, retries, cost-meter, SLA tracking)

verdict: The pipeline is brittle because it treats stages as a DAG of hopes instead of a schema-validated, frame-locked, single-pass contract — fix the render and contracts first, everything else falls in line.
